chunks: And from him, by his chain, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, he said: And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Muhsin ibn Ahmad al-Maythami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him say:
Indeed, Iblis has a devil called Haz', who fills what is between the East and the West every night, coming to people in their sleep.

key_terms.إبليس: Iblis, the chief of the devils who refused to prostrate to Adam
key_terms.المنام: Sleep/dreams, the state in which people are visited by this devil
key_terms.شيطان: Shaytan (devil), a demonic entity serving under Iblis
key_terms.هزع: Haz', proper name of a specific devil under Iblis

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the devil of dreams called Haz'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes a particular devil in the service of Iblis named Haz', whose vast form spans from East to West and whose function is to visit people during their dreams every night. This teaching, delivered to Abu Basir, was part of the Imam's broader instruction about the unseen realm and the mechanisms through which satanic influence operates, particularly through the vulnerability of the sleeping state.

en.bilal-muhammad: And from him by his isnad from `Ali b. al Hakam from Aban b. `Uthman. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abu’l Khattab narrated to me from Muhsin b. Ahmad al-Maythami from Aban b. `Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Ja`far (as).  He said: I heard him say:
Surely, there is a devil for Iblis known as Haz` (هزع) who fills up what is between the East and the West every night. He comes to them in [their] sleep.
